Dear Sister Lauterbach:
The word is out that you are hanging up your wings and putting away your rolling
suitcase. After 42 years of helping curious, nervous and sometimes obnoxious passengers
to feel comfortable in the sky, you are going to enjoy life in the beautiful city on the bay.
All of your friends in the labor movement join me in wishing you many pleasant
years of full-time relaxation and pursuit of purely personal pleasures; you deserve them.
career, you were never content simply to watch the world whiz
by the cabin windows.
During your lon ou helped make changes, changes for the better for co-workers
and many others by your leadership in building the organization that is now the
Association of Flight Attendants.
You proved that a trade union is an instrument for
bringing dignity, fairness and gender equality to the work place.
We were especially proud and pleased that you took part in the ceremony when
the American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations issued its
charter of affiliation to the AFA, a milestone in the honored history of the labor
movement.
Good luck and best wishes!
Sincerely and fraternally,
Same Pille O
President
